acceptance: Every reader of each of the three artifacts is listed (rollback, rehearsal, automatic rollback decision, visual or other checks), with file and step.
Retention of site-artifact equals the recorded rollback window; the other two artifacts use the shortest retention their readers need.
A rollback dispatched to a deploy inside the new window succeeds on the real workflow (rehearsal target), and a deploy still passes end to end.
Site Actions storage measured before and 14 days after; recorded here.
context:
Decision gate: Owner decision required before changing site-artifact retention: how far back must a rollback reach (for example 14, 30 or 90 days)? Default if no answer: keep 90 days for site-artifact and change only the other artifacts and the npm cache.

Item guardrails: Never break rollback; do not delete existing artifacts by hand; no change to deploy targets, certification gates or the automatic rollback decision; one site PR.

Verification rubric: Pass = readers list complete, rehearsal rollback succeeds, storage numbers recorded. Fail = any rollback inside the decided window cannot find its artifact.

Base guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight), never the primary clone; one PR per repository; no live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs; heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, servers) only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status; never start deliberate CPU, memory or disk load, and tests inject readings instead; comment policy (make comment-policy-check); changelog.d fragment for user-facing change. Re-verify every cited file and line on current develop before acting; they are hints and drift. Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review is re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Origin: Found 2026-11-17 by the egress root-cause investigation; premise corrected the same day after reading deploy.yml.

Owner decision 2026-11-17: rollback window is 14 days. site-artifact retention-days = 14; the other two deploy artifacts use the shortest retention their readers need; npm cache restored only where npm runs.
description:
Problem: each BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site deploy uploads site-artifact-<run> (~126 MB) and two other artifacts with retention-days 90 (deploy.yml ~96-109 and ~177-181) and restores a ~236 MB npm cache in two jobs (setup-node cache npm, ~57 and ~140), about 8 deploys a day. Site Actions storage grew from 73.9 to 105.7 GB between 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-16. Correction to the first version of this item: the `gh run download` of site-artifact-<run> (~84) runs only in rollback mode, to restore an earlier deploy; it is not a second download in a normal deploy. So the 90-day retention is the rollback window, and cutting it limits how far back a rollback can go.

Outcome: the rollback window is a recorded decision, retention matches it, artifacts that no rollback or check reads use short retention, and the npm cache is restored only by jobs that run npm.
